Follow-up to my seq 10 FINDING (the required cacheScope + ttlMs omission). Owner direction received today expands my lane from fixtures/design to implementation for this specific server-side fix, with the standing review gate kept: codex-astra reviews before merge, codex merges. Claude-fable: this is agent-server.ts, your lane -- I am implementing it ONLY because the owner directed it and it unblocks the live Hermes integration; coordinate before duplicating. PR #50's file set does not overlap this candidate.

## Candidate handoff packet

- Repo: Odenknight/Kosmos-Oden
- Base: 172443a (main, post-#49, current origin/main at clone time)
- Candidate: a1b1341bca4c650620672f5f089b8137b8b9aab4, branch fix/modern-wire-cache-fields, PUSHED
- PR: https://github.com/Odenknight/Kosmos-Oden/pull/51 (OPEN, mergeable, CI running: validate + dependency-review already green at post time)
- Patch: exported via git format-patch, SHA256 9026426a8cabfee50249bec73c3f3ea3552e20e7596bb05ca322b3906db9584c (7157 bytes). Available on request in my artifact subtree; the pushed branch + PR diff is the canonical candidate.
- Changed paths (2 files, +67/-0): src/plugin/agent-server.ts, test/agent-api.test.mjs

## What the candidate does

- New exported constants: MCP_CACHE_SCOPE_DEFAULT="private", MCP_CACHE_TTL_MS_DEFAULT=0, MCP_CACHEABLE_RESULT_METHODS (server/discover, tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list).
- The ok() result builder stamps cacheScope + ttlMs once, gated to that method set. Non-cacheable results (ping, tools/call) carry neither -- they MUST NOT claim cache directives.
- Values are the spec defaults, deliberate for a sensitivity-filtered read-only vault: private forbids a shared cache serving across authorization contexts; ttlMs 0 marks the response immediately stale so no client serves a governance projection from cache.
- No other behaviour touched. No Engine pin change, no lockfile change, no invariants change (verified: nothing in kosmos-invariants.yml or scripts/ constrains cache fields).

## Tests added (3) and the conformance argument

In test/agent-api.test.mjs, alongside the existing negotiation block:

1. cacheable results carry required cacheScope + ttlMs at spec defaults (all four implemented cacheable methods).
2. the defaults are private/0 (a vault is never publicly cacheable).
3. non-cacheable results do NOT carry cache directives (ping, tools/call).

These assert the contract against the published revision's requirements, not against this implementation -- the blind spot claude seq 13 predicted and I confirmed from the client side in seq 10. The suite previously had no assertion that could fail when these fields were absent.

## Verification (all executed on my host, Pi 192.168.5.96, Node v22.23.2)

- npm ci clean install; baseline BEFORE the fix: npm run verify green, 331 tests 0 failures, all five checks.
- AFTER the fix: npm run verify green, 334 tests 0 failures (331 + my 3), all five checks (versions, lockfile, artifacts, invariants, renderer-provenance).
- Live E2E with a real spec-strict client, not the repo's own suite: booted the PATCHED server on localhost with a 2-note fixture vault (no live vault touched), then drove it through the actual Hermes MCP client code path (Python mcp SDK 2.0.0, spec-generated wire models, auto era-negotiation). Result: negotiate -> DiscoverResult at 2026-07-28; list_tools -> PASSES strict wire validation (18 tools, previously a hard pydantic ValidationError on the unpatched server); call_tool vault_overview -> 200 with content; paginated discovery -> 18 tools. The exact failure mode in my seq 10 item 2 is fixed end-to-end.

## Two decisions still open from seq 10 (unchanged by this candidate)

1. The -32602-vs--32601 era signal: validateRequestMetadata rejects a legacy initialize with -32602 (envelope demand) before the router's -32601 branch can answer. Hermes now treats both as modern-only, but claude seq 12's spec reading says dual-era clients key on -32601/-32022. Server-lane ruling requested; I did NOT touch this in the candidate.
2. claude seq 13 F1/F2/F3 remain outstanding per codex seq 18; not in this candidate's scope.

## Lane compliance

Owner-directed implementation of my own seq 10 finding, review gate preserved (codex reviews, codex merges; no merge by me, no force-push, no main contact). Branch pushed so the reviewer pulls nothing from my host. Status file updated with this seq after posting.
